clue.text: Year chap's at sea in tub, a submarine vessel

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside that other word
being at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: chap plus the S of the possessive
to tub is to wash in a bath
Y is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A man spends a year adrift in a little tub, as if it were a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tub' looks like a noun, a little boat, but it is a verb meaning to wash in a bath; the shuffled year and chap letters sit inside that verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathyscaphe is a free-diving craft built for deep-sea exploration, the vessel that took people to the ocean floor.

clue.text: No limits to ritual about demigod

indicators.note: without its limits a word loses its outermost letters at both ends
turned about suggests the letters are moved around into a different order

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters stripped away

explanation.surface: A comment that a ritual centred on a demigod has no restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip RITUAL of its ends to get ITUA, then rearrange it as AITU.
explanation.definitionFit: In Polynesian belief an aitu is a spirit or minor deity, so a semi-divine being fits the clue's demigod.

clue.text: Aviation fuel? Whack in poor stuff

indicators.note: something put in another word is placed inside it

parts.note: tripe is slang for rubbish or worthless material
to tan someone is to beat or thrash them

explanation.surface: Someone is told to throw any old rubbish into an aircraft's fuel tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whack' is a verb meaning to beat, and 'poor stuff' means rubbish. The question mark admits that triptane is an anti-knock additive in aviation fuel rather than the fuel itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Triptane is a hydrocarbon with high octane rating, blended into aircraft engine petrol to prevent knocking.

clue.text: Husband quite close to wife's big toe

indicators.note: being close to something means sitting right beside it, so the pieces are set side by side

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband
as in 'all alone', meaning quite alone
UX is the abbreviation for the Latin uxor, a wife

explanation.surface: A husband lies very close to his wife's big toe.
explanation.walkthrough: UX stands for uxor, Latin for wife, a dictionary abbreviation; the 's simply joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallux is the anatomical name for the innermost digit of the foot in humans.

clue.text: Hints working with US people confined to home?

indicators.note: something working is being processed or worked over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: US looks like a label for the people, but its letters join the anagram; the question mark flags the American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English, shut-ins are invalids or recluses who stay indoors, unable or unwilling to go out.

clue.text: Number chasing projection about international money once

parts.note: a cog is a tooth projecting from a wheel
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.walkthrough: 'projection' wants to be the definition, since a coign is a projecting corner, but here it is COG; the definition is 'money once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coign is an obsolete spelling of coin, so it once meant currency as well as a jutting corner.

clue.text: Hunter to operate a long time

parts.note: to act is to function or operate
an aeon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A hunter takes ages to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: Actaeon is the hunter of Greek myth who saw Artemis bathing and was turned into a stag.
explanation.definitionFit: Actaeon is a famous huntsman from Greek legend, killed by his own hounds after his transformation.

clue.text: Transmit internet messaging everywhere

parts.note: to pass something on is to transmit it
the initial letters of instant messaging, the online chat service

explanation.surface: Online chat spreads messages all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: Passim is Latin, used in footnotes to say a reference occurs throughout a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim marks a term or idea found throughout a book, at many places, hence widely scattered.

clue.text: I can finally replace defective legacy computer

indicators.note: something defective is faulty and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the next word, keeping only its closing letter

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: An IT worker boasts that they can at last swap out a faulty old machine.
explanation.walkthrough: ENIAC, built in 1945, was one of the first general-purpose electronic computers.
explanation.definitionFit: ENIAC was a pioneering valve-based machine from the 1940s, an early ancestor of modern computing hardware.

clue.text: Scottish sailors rest on first sign of breathing fumes

parts.note: to tarry is to linger or stay

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
reeks is Scots for smoke or fumes

explanation.surface: Scots seamen take a break as soon as they smell smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarry-breeks, literally tarred trousers, is an old Scots nickname for a sailor; the plural reading of the phrase is fair because the word serves for one or many.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors once tarred their clothing for waterproofing, so Scots called a seaman by his tar-stained breeches.

clue.text: Performing gig band's following sweet pieces of good fortune

clue.text: Group of porpoises mainly fine crossing choppy ocean

explanation.definitionFit: Phocaena is the zoological genus containing the harbour porpoise, a taxonomic group of these small cetaceans.

clue.text: Profitable source of revenue extracted from titanium oxide

clue.text: Make gathers in lining of top

clue.text: Twisting hand to enable throw of double six?

clue.text: Bats urinated poisonous alkaloid

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bats relieved themselves, producing a toxic substance.

clue.text: About to get the better of worry that's consuming one, like a tapeworm?

as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside DO IN, then EAT is added and the whole lot is reversed. 'consuming' fits the tapeworm picture but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Taenia is the tapeworm genus, and the suffix -oid means resembling, so this describes something ribbon-like.

clue.text: Cinema's presentation's very long promoting independence

explanation.walkthrough: I stands for independent; moving it from the end of MAXI to the start gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: IMAX is a format of giant-screen projection, shown in specially built theatres.

clue.text: Helmet's base moulded with tin

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Search screening a rector's ecclesiastical successor
